decisions.decision: Assessors will carry mace and stay on the same street (not necessarily the same property) together for safety while inspecting chapter-land parcels.
The office will explore using the police boat to inspect lakefront properties rather than entering by land.
The pending 41A appellant must submit a complete, signed application and bank documentation well ahead of any board meeting, not at the last minute.
Direction given to continue pursuing a seasonal employee, through the town manager, to help with neighborhood-review corrections rather than finalizing a scope of work now.
Board will move forward with the in-house senior-exemption brochure design rather than wait further for the volunteer-drafted version, given the September 3rd deadline.
Discussion of Clause 18 exemption criteria postponed until the fall.
Status of DOR directives will be folded into the regular status report from the principal assessor rather than kept as a separate agenda item.
Per town counsel's guidance, discussion of chapter-land liens and roll-back taxes on specific parcels will be held in open/public session, not executive session.

minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed a lengthy office status report covering chapter-land liens, roll-back taxes, cyclical inspections, and a response to a two-year-old Select Board investigation, then spent much of the meeting reconciling parcel counts before signing FY2026 preliminary real estate, personal property and motor vehicle excise tax warrants. what_happened.line: Assessors signed the FY2026 preliminary real estate and personal property tax warrants after reconciling mismatched parcel counts between the town's Munis system and the state LA4 filing.
The board voted to release the parcel at 222 West Townsend Road from chapter-land status, clearing it for potential sale.
The board also signed two motor vehicle excise commitment warrants covering separate batches of bills.
Staffing shortages are limiting field inspections; the office is weighing carrying mace on site visits, using the police boat for lakefront parcels, and adding a seasonal employee.
The board opted to move forward with an in-house design for the senior means-tested tax exemption brochure to meet a September 3rd deadline.

why_it_matters: Signing the preliminary tax warrant sets the real estate, personal property, and motor vehicle excise bills that get mailed to residents this cycle.
A parcel leaving chapter-land status changes what that property owner can do with the land and how it's taxed going forward.
The senior means-tested exemption brochure and application, due by September 3rd, affects which seniors can apply for reduced tax bills this year.
